Order 
This is first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 read with Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (herein after referred to as the Code) for grant of bail relating to FIR No.63 of 2024 (date not mentioned) registered at Police Station Kurawar, District Rajgarh (MP) for offence punishable under Sections 376 (2) (n),
376 (3) and 506-II of Indian Penal Code, 1908, under Section 3 read with Section 4 (2) of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and also under Section 3 (1) (w) (ii) and 3 (2) (v) of Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.

sentences.text: The applicant is in jail since 22.02.2024.

2. As per prosecution, the allegation against the applicant is that he abducted the prosecutrix (a m i n o r g i r l ) a n d f o r c e f u l l y c o m m i t t e d r a p e u p o n N E U T R A L C I T A T I O N N O .
2024:MPHC-IND:26396 2 MCRC-39206-2024 her.
After lodging of the complaint, the applicant has been implicated in the present offence and has been arrested.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the alleged offence.

He has further submitted that in this case as per statement recorded first time under Section 164 of the Code, the prosecutrix has admitted that she was in love relationship with the present applicant; and further in this case statement of the prosecutrix has been recorded before the trial Court in which last two sentences of para 6 are significant wherein she Deepak vs The State Of M.P. on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62088440/
1 has stated that when her mother has lodged report against the present applicant, she had demanded Rs.6,00,000/- (rupees six lakhs only).

entities.text: Deepak vs The State Of M.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, she stated that it is true to say that the applicant was ready to deposit Rs.3,00,000/- (rupees three lakhs only), but since the demanded amount of Rs.6,00,000/- (rupees six lakhs only) has not been paid, the report was lodged.
The applicant is aged around 22 years and he is in custody since 22.02.2024 i.e. more than seven months.
The investigation is complete and the charge sheet has already been filed.
The trial will take time for its conclusion.
On these grounds, prayer for grant of bail to the applicant has been made.
4. Learned Government Advocate has opposed the bail application.
5. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

6. On due consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case, so also the fact that the prosecutrix was having love relations with the applicant and also the custody period of the applicant and trial will take considerable NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:26396 3 MCRC-39206-2024 time for its conclusion, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application filed by the applicant is allowed.

Applicant - Deepak son of Mangu @ Mangilal is directed to be released on bail upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/ -(Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the court concerned during trial and shall also abide by the conditions enumerated under Section 437 (3) of the Code.
7. This order shall be effective till the end of the trial, however, in case of bail jump, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.
